item.title: $2m water profit | Water bottler posts six months results
item.description: PUBLICLY-LISTED producer and bottler of VaiWai Natural Artesian water and AquaSafe – Pleass Global Limited – has recorded a profit before tax of $2,590,069 for the six months ended June 30 this year. That represents a 17 per cent increase over the $2,208,333 recorded for the corresponding period in 2025.
item.content:encoded:
PUBLICLY-LISTED producer and bottler of VaiWai Natural Artesian water and AquaSafe – Pleass Global Limited – has recorded a profit before tax of $2,590,069 for the six months ended June 30 this year.

That represents a 17 per cent increase over the $2,208,333 recorded for the corresponding period in 2025.

Revenue also increased by 19 per cent to $16,087,964, which the company said reflected continued growth across the business and the strength of the company’s brands and operations.

Company chairman and joint chief executive officer Warwick Pleass said the company’s financial position continued to strengthen, with net assets increasing to $40.5 million as at June 30, 2026, compared with $33.1m recorded at the same time last year.

He said the company board had also approved an interim dividend of 10 cents a share, up from eight cents per share in the first half of 2025.

“These results reflect the continued dedication of our people, the strength of our brands, and the confidence our customers and stakeholders continue to place in Pleass Global,” Mr Pleass said in the company’s stock market announcement.

“Achieving strong revenue and profit growth, together with declaring an interim dividend of 10 cents per share, demonstrates the strength of our long-term strategy and our commitment to creating sustainable value for shareholders.

“We thank our employees, customers, suppliers and shareholders for their ongoing support.

“Based on our current performance and outlook, we remain confident in the company’s continued growth and future prospects.”

item.title: Five-star resort retains ISO status
item.description: FIVE-STAR resort Shangri-La Yanuca Island has retained its status as Fiji’s only resort certified for its Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) system and the internationally recognised ISO 22000:2018 Food Safety Management System. The globally recognised food safety system establishes rigorous controls for identifying, managing and preventing potential food safety risks across culina
item.content:encoded:
FIVE-STAR resort Shangri-La Yanuca Island has retained its status as Fiji’s only resort certified for its Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) system and the internationally recognised ISO 22000:2018 Food Safety Management System.

The globally recognised food safety system establishes rigorous controls for identifying, managing and preventing potential food safety risks across culinary operations.

Having successfully achieved recertification, the resort said reaffirmed its position as the country’s only resort certified to this internationally recognised food safety standard.

Resort general manager Francis Lee said following a stringent independent audit process, the recertification confirmed that comprehensive food safety practices remained embedded across the resort’s culinary process, from ingredient sourcing and receiving through preparation, service and ongoing monitoring.

“Achieving ISO 22000:2018 recertification is a significant milestone for Shangri-La Yanuca Island and reflects the dedication, teamwork and care demonstrated by our colleagues across the resort,” Mr Lee said in a statement from the resort.

“As Fiji’s only resort certified to ISO 22000:2018, we are proud to give our guests added confidence that every dining experience is supported by the highest standards of care and quality.”

Mr Lee said the certification extended beyond the resort’s seven restaurants and bars to include all colleague dining facilities and operational kitchens, covering a total of 15 food and beverage outlets.

He said their hygiene and sanitation team worked closely with colleagues across culinary, stewarding, purchasing and operations to ensure rigorous food safety practices were consistently upheld.

“As Fiji’s only resort certified to ISO 22000:2018, Shangri-La Yanuca Island, Fiji continues to set a benchmark for food safety excellence in Fiji’s hospitality industry, combining internationally recognized standards with authentic Fijian hospitality.”

In 2001, the Shangri-La Group introduced the Shangri-La Food Safety (SFS) Management System, developed around internationally recognised HACCP principles.

And since 2023, Shangri-La properties have further strengthened this commitment through ISO 22000:2018 Food Safety Management System certification, reinforcing a culture of continuous improvement and internationally recognised food safety practices.

item.title: Clothing chain expands to Rakiraki
item.description: POPULAR retail chain for second-hand and preloved items Value City has opened its 16th shop in Rakiraki. The new shop is located at Bhima Holdings Building behind Lums Hot Bread Shop in Rakiraki town.
item.content:encoded:
POPULAR retail chain for second-hand and preloved items Value City has opened its 16th shop in Rakiraki.

The new shop is located at Bhima Holdings Building behind Lums Hot Bread Shop in Rakiraki town.

Value City marketing and public relations manager Monica Chute said the location is ideal as it is opposite the market and the bus stand, which allows them to serve those who come in from nearby communities.

“Previously, people had to travel to Tavua or Ba to shop and due to the fuel crisis and increased transportation costs now, this has allowed us to serve those who come in from nearby villages and settlements,” she said.

She said approximately $60000 has been invested and five people have been employed.

Ms Chute said the new shop was opened early this month due to public demand and offers all its popular products including recycled clothing, shoes, bags, jewellery, bric-a-brac, household ware, glassware and camping gear.

She said they are also upgrading their systems and are undergoing a digital transformation whereby Operations, Inventory, Finance and Human Resources management are undergoing strategic technological changes.

Value City currently has outlets in Nausori, Nakasi, Challenge Plaza LBE, Nabua, Regal Building Suva, Lami, Navua, Sigatoka, Namaka Nadi, Lautoka, Ba, Tavua, Rakiraki, Taveuni, Savusavu and Labasa and will be further expanding to Seaqaqa, Korovou and Tailevu.

She said the rise in fuel costs and freights charges have also affected the business as they get their supplies from Australia and New Zealand.

“The rising cost of fuel has significantly increased our freight and operating expenses, making it more expensive to move stock across Fiji while keeping our prices affordable for customers,” she said.

She said some of the challenges faced are adapting to the ever-changing business environment, shortage of skilled and unskilled labor due to migration of workers and difficulty in finding and retaining reliable staff.

She said remittances from abroad have also disrupted the local workforce with high rates of absenteeism and lack of motivation in the workforce.

Ms Chute said to cope, they implemented cost-cutting measures within the organisation.

She said they are also upgrading their systems and are undergoing a digital transformation whereby Operations, Inventory, Finance and Human Resources management are undergoing strategic technological changes.

She said they also look forward to creating more awareness and advocacy for the importance of recycling and re-using, reducing waste and what goes into our landfills and the importance of shopping for recycled goods.

item.title: Lau women seek to protect heritage
item.description: THE Soqosoqo ni marama ko Lau held a first Lau Intellectual Property Awareness Workshop at the Yatu Lau Conference Centre in Suva last Thursday. It brought together women, youth, and men from across Lau to learn how to safeguard their crafts, knowledge and creativity through patents, trademarks and geographical indications.
item.content:encoded:
THE Soqosoqo ni marama ko Lau held a first Lau Intellectual Property Awareness Workshop at the Yatu Lau Conference Centre in Suva last Thursday.

It brought together women, youth, and men from across Lau to learn how to safeguard their crafts, knowledge and creativity through patents, trademarks and geographical indications.

For years, people of Lau have raised concerns that their traditional knowledge, designs and ideas have been exploited, abused, and misused for the monetary gain of others.

Speaking at the workshop, Acting Solicitor-General Iliesa Tuiloma said cultural heritage goes beyond money.

Mr Tuiloma said traditional knowledge was important.

“It’s very significant because it has not only the social and financial effect,” he said.

“It also follows through with some spiritual and the feelings and that’s what outsiders don’t realise how important this traditional knowledge and cultural expression is.”

“We know that kava has already been now patented by German as well as US companies.

“The second one is most of the products that we have, for example, the tanoa now has been registered in the US.”

He said a new Bill, which was tabled in Parliament in September following public consultations is aimed at protecting Lau resources and ending what many call daylight robbery “of their sacred knowledge, art and designs”.

Mr Tuiloma added the public complaints had led to the drafting of the proposed Bill which has been welcomed by a majority of those who were part of the public consultations.

item.title: Women empowered through AI training
item.description: WOMEN in Tech Fiji, in partnership with the Ministry for Women, Children and Social Protection, successfully hosted the Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Women Professionals event, equipping women with practical knowledge and skills to confidently use artificial intelligence in the workplace. Facilitated by Eventuros Fiji in Nadi, the free hands-on workshop brought together women professionals from
item.content:encoded:
WOMEN in Tech Fiji, in partnership with the Ministry for Women, Children and Social Protection, successfully hosted the Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Women Professionals event, equipping women with practical knowledge and skills to confidently use artificial intelligence in the workplace.

Facilitated by Eventuros Fiji in Nadi, the free hands-on workshop brought together women professionals from a range of industries to explore how AI can improve productivity, creativity, and everyday work processes.

Participants were introduced to key AI concepts, prompt engineering, everyday AI tools, research and knowledge management, content and presentation creation, creative AI applications, responsible AI use, and practical demonstrations designed to help them apply these tools in their own roles.

The initiative reflects a shared commitment by Women in Tech Fiji, the Ministry for Women, Children and Social Protection, and Eventuros Fiji to empower more women with the digital skills needed to thrive in an increasingly AI-driven workforce.

The event also featured the Women in Tech Fiji membership drive, encouraging more women to connect, learn and grow through a supportive network focused on technology, innovation, and professional development.

item.title: Nawaikula reveals details on new proposed People’s Star Network Party
item.description: Former Member of Parliament Niko Nawaikula has publicly declared his support for the proposed People’s Star Network Party, saying he will help promote and advise the party despite being barred from contesting the next general election. In a social media post, Mr Nawaikula said a recent photograph of him alongside party promoter Tau Eliki and supporters was intended to demonstrate his backing for t
item.content:encoded:
Former Member of Parliament Niko Nawaikula has publicly declared his support for the proposed People’s Star Network Party, saying he will help promote and advise the party despite being barred from contesting the next general election.

In a social media post, Mr Nawaikula said a recent photograph of him alongside party promoter Tau Eliki and supporters was intended to demonstrate his backing for the proposed political party.

Mr Nawaikula said he is unable to contest the next election because of his 2022 conviction and the provisions of Fiji’s electoral laws.

“The Electoral Act does not allow me to contest this election on account of my conviction in 2022. Even the Political Parties Registration & Disclosures Act does not allow me to be the applicant or holder of a proposed party executive or signatory,” he said.

He described the restrictions as “harsh and sad”, noting that he had already served his sentence.

“Rather harsh and sad especially when you consider I have served my punishment but that is the law that must be respected.”

Mr Nawaikula said the law does not prevent him from supporting, promoting or becoming a member of the proposed party, or from assisting it if it is registered.

“The same law does not stop me from being a supporter or promoter or being a party member or being invited to help or do any work for the proposed party now or if it’s approved.”

He said he had reviewed the party’s proposed constitution and supported its provisions, including mechanisms to discipline or remove Members of Parliament who failed to comply with party rules.

Mr Nawaikula also said the proposed party would serve as the political arm of an independent association of vanua and chiefs, which would remain separate and apolitical.

He claimed he had been sidelined by both the People’s Alliance Party (PAP) and SODELPA, but said the proposed People’s Star Network Party had invited him to work closely with it if it gains registration.

“To all who support me and the issues I advocate please support this effort so that what we advocate are not just talk and can materialise into actions,” he said.

The proposed People’s Star Network Party is currently collecting signatures as part of the registration process required under Fiji’s electoral laws.

item.title: EFL executive pay rises to $3.76M in 2025
item.description: Compensation paid to Energy Fiji Limited’s (EFL) key management personnel increased to $3.756 million in 2025, according to the company’s 2025 Annual Report recently tabled in Parliament. The report shows total remuneration for the Chief Executive Officer and Executive Management Group rose from $3.309 million in 2024 to $3.756 million in 2025, an increase of $447,000, or about 13.5 per cent.
item.content:encoded:
Compensation paid to Energy Fiji Limited’s (EFL) key management personnel increased to $3.756 million in 2025, according to the company’s 2025 Annual Report recently tabled in Parliament.

The report shows total remuneration for the Chief Executive Officer and Executive Management Group rose from $3.309 million in 2024 to $3.756 million in 2025, an increase of $447,000, or about 13.5 per cent.

Salary, performance pay and allowances accounted for $3.445 million, up from $3.033 million the previous year.

Superannuation contributions also increased, rising from $276,000 in 2024 to $311,000 in 2025.

The report identifies the Chief Executive Officer and Executive Management Group as the company’s key management personnel responsible for planning, directing and controlling EFL’s operations.

Fatiaki Gibson was appointed Chief Executive Officer in April 2025.

The executive management team also includes Deputy Chief Executive Officer Mitsuhiro Takeshita, Chief Operating Officer Bobby Naimawi, Chief Financial Officer Semisi Tawake, General Manager Generation Epeli Malo, General Manager Customer Services Annabel Ducia, General Manager Network Jitendra V. Kumar, General Manager Human Resources Randhir Charan, General Manager System Planning and Control Naomi Baleca, General Manager Information Technology Jiten Singh, and General Manager Special Projects Krishneel Prasad.

The annual report also details changes to the EFL Board during the year.

Rokoseru Nabalarua served as Chairman, while Mitsuhiro Takeshita joined the Board in June 2025 and Toshiyuki Suzuki was appointed in September 2025.

During the year, Fatiaki Gibson resigned as a director in March 2025, while Chitoshi Fukuda resigned in August 2025 and Tsutomu Fujita stepped down in June 2025.

Director fees paid during 2025 totalled $68,250, compared with $46,542 in 2024.

item.title: Registered voters reach 707,982 after latest roll update
item.description: The Fijian Elections Office (FEO) says the country’s National Register of Voters now stands at 707,982 registered voters, following its latest update completed in January 2026. Figures released by the FEO show the latest exercise reviewed data covering the period July to December 2025.
item.content:encoded:
The Fijian Elections Office (FEO) says the country’s National Register of Voters now stands at 707,982 registered voters, following its latest update completed in January 2026.

Figures released by the FEO show the latest exercise reviewed data covering the period July to December 2025.

During the update, 3,442 deceased persons were removed from the register, 484 individuals were flagged as inmates, 34 voters were reinstated and two people were removed after renouncing their Fijian citizenship.

The latest update follows a series of voter roll verification exercises conducted since July 2023.

According to the data, the number of registered voters has generally increased over the period, rising from 695,435 in July 2023 to 707,982 in January 2026, despite ongoing efforts to remove deceased voters and update the register.

Since July 2023, the FEO has removed a total of 30,123 deceased persons from the National Register of Voters.

Over the same period, 733 individuals have been flagged as inmates, 190 voters have been reinstated after verification, and 10 people have been removed after renouncing their Fijian citizenship.

The FEO noted that its July 2025 verification exercise included a four-phase deceased voter verification process using information from the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registry (BDM), the Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF), the Provisional Voters List (PVL) together with Turaga ni Koro and next-of-kin verification.

The office said the BDM and FNPF data used in that exercise covered records from 2012 to June 2025 as part of efforts to maintain the accuracy and integrity of the National Register of Voters.
